comments.author: @davidbayliss3789
comments.text:
I didn’t learn Latin as a kid, though my partner did. Apparently, it’s still taught in some schools (both classical Latin, with assumed pronunciations based on poetry and Romance languages, and the Italian-influenced Ecclesiastical Latin). I'm 51 now, and while I can't pinpoint exactly when or where, I'm familiar with how to pronounce many Latinisms. I wonder if that's because I was drawn to tech and science as a kid, which influenced my reading, or if it’s more about age demographics and cultural exposure. Maybe it’s even geographical—perhaps younger people in the UK still encounter Latin more often than in other English-speaking countries? (And I'd imagine that in Latin-derived language countries, people are even more familiar with classical expressions.)

I find myself a bit surprised when Wes doesn’t seem to know some of these small things intuitively—I’d just assume he’d have come across them more through science/techy interests. Maybe it’s an American thing?
